para.text: calculates where the line connecting two neighboring cells intersects the cell face between them. It then calculates what fraction of the length of the cell face is on each side of the intersection point and returns the minimum value it calculates for any of the neighboring cells. If the line intersection point is not along the line segment connecting the two cells, Min_Crossing_Fraction can be negative.

In an ideal DISV mesh, the minimum crossing fraction would be 0.5 for all cells. However, if the cell centers of both neighboring cells are both on the edge of the grid, a minimum crossing fraction of zero would be ideal.

image.caption: The length of the red line divided by the length of the solid blue line would be the crossing fraction for the two cells on either side of the solid blue line.
